sources.finding: Old HTML defaults to backend=rmt and multi=0 because checkbox unchecked.
Current deployed HTML defaults backend=rmt and always sends multi=1.
backend=library invokes learnWithLibrary; backend=rmt invokes learnSignal; multi=0 skips multi-frame extension when valid first frame received.
Batch uses payload={'multi':'1','backend': backend} for both rmt and library; prompts Enter before initiating HTTP request; timeout 14s.

confirmed_static_findings: Old default HTML test is not equivalent to new matrix batch because RMT single-frame multi=0 versus matrix multi=1.

Current deployed HTML rmt/multi=1 and batch rmt/multi=1 do use same server endpoint, form parameters and backend. Source alone cannot explain differing real-world outcomes under otherwise identical conditions.
Client timeout 14s exceeds nominal server 5s learning window; actual HTTP 408 is explicitly sent by firmware upon !received, not urllib socket timeout.
Backend=library requires disabling ESP-IDF RMT and enabling IRremoteESP8266 interrupt-based receiver, an additional difference from old HTML rmt default.
Adding GPIO pin probe and reflashing is diagnostic instrumentation, not proven necessary fix for failure of batch.
indeterminate: Whether old HTML success refers to first-frame reception or successful lamp color change.
Real physical GPIO5 edges, libraryLastRawLength, rxLastSymbolCount for failed tests without the detailed device error JSON.
Whether request trigger-to-button timing differs enough to affect captures.
True cause of all reported zero-capture outcomes.
corrective_actions: Do not attribute failure to GPIO5 hardware from HTTP 408 alone.
Do not flash diagnostic firmware before establishing parity of known working old HTML request.
Reproduce old HTML baseline with backend=rmt,multi=0; compare against deployed UI backend=rmt,multi=1; inspect exact 408 response body and avoid extra backend unless needed.
Add static UI-versus-CLI API contract regression to prevent drift.

conclusions: GPIO5 and RMT hardware path are demonstrably capable of receiving a valid full-remote frame under baseline conditions
HTTP 408 can occur intermittently under same nominal backend and multi=0 settings; do not attribute to hardware faults or multi flag alone
Need capture warm and dim with backend=rmt and multi=0 as next logical test before using extra multi-frame sequences
Do not treat successful transmit driver calls or lighting blink as proof that color/brightness changed

source_analysis: handleLearn assigns lastSignal = move(captured), and handleSendLast forwards lastSignal into transmitSignal() and transmitFrame(signal, signal.pulses). No command-ID substitution occurs in this path.
transmitFrame reproduces pulse signs and microsecond durations as RMT level-duration symbols, splitting values only above 32767us (none in observed first frame).
DRIVER_OK reports RMT HAL return, not optical readback; verified_by_receiver=false.
tx_duration_ms=4065 unexpectedly differs from captured pulse sum 64.881 ms; requires exact stage timing and independent receiving ESP32.
